arm_tapped.why_this_screen: adding 100+ graph outputs can change partitioning. The VERDICT is computed on the untapped run; the taps only feed the liveness bar. If a tapped output is not bit-identical to its untapped twin, the liveness bar is describing a different run and says so here

arm_untapped.note: the graph criterion 10 actually runs, with no taps added

not_done_here: atol and rtol are not moved -- fifth round running
no criterion-10 row is closed; the verdict stays whatever the criterion says
nothing that follows from this answer is proposed

predictions.chain_vs_both_eps: the chain should sit closer to both EPs than the EPs sit to each other only if their errors are uncorrelated; correlated rounding would put it outside them
predictions.note: A PREDICTION IS NOT A READING (docs/DESIGN.md §8.9.24(6)). Recorded so the measurements can contradict them. I was the specimen for this rule one round ago.
predictions.output_0: the isolated lm_head put ORT's CPU EP further from true (2 vs 11 ULP). At model scale the Vulkan EP additionally carries 32 layers of its own drift, so I expect this to be able to reverse -- and if it does NOT reverse that is the more interesting reading
predictions.outputs_63_64: round 37 established both EPs are BIT-EXACT on these with identical inputs, so at model scale their distance from true should be whatever their layer-31 QKV inputs already carried -- inherited, and I do not predict a direction
predictions.what_would_make_this_inconclusive: any layer failing its liveness bar, any arm with a zero dispatch or claim delta, or the two reference variants (f64 / f16r) disagreeing on direction

question: for criterion 10's outputs 0, 63 and 64 AS THE CRITERION SEES THEM -- each EP's own in-situ output on the whole model -- which of the two is further from the true value?

reference_variants.f16r: each node's exact result rounded once to fp16 before the next node
reference_variants.f64: exact real arithmetic of the composed graph, no intermediate rounding
reference_variants.why_both: 'true' has two defensible readings at fp16 and neither is privileged; where they agree on direction the answer is robust to the choice, and where they disagree the disagreement is the finding

ruling: docs/DESIGN.md §8.9.24(4), the half round 37 costed and did not run

seam_honesty.chain_never_reads: any EP-computed tensor, at any layer boundary
seam_honesty.chain_reads: initialisers, input_ids, and the rotary caches (constants, checked bit-equal between the two EPs' taps before use)
seam_honesty.liveness_reads: both EPs' taps, per layer, per side -- and its result never reaches the chain
seam_honesty.why_this_is_the_answer_to_arm_f: arm F was dishonest because a reference seeded from one side was compared against the other side's output. Here the reference is a function of the weights alone: neither side appears in its derivation, so neither side can be favoured by its construction

selector_caveat: a selector is a request, not an identity; device_name is off the run

cpu_ep_vs_reference.allowance_in_ulps_at_scale_basis: (atol=0.001 + rtol=0.02*|b|) / one_ulp_at_scale=0.0078125, evaluated at each element's own reference over every element. This is the WHOLE predicate allowance; atol_in_ulps_at_scale is one term of it and must never be quoted as the tolerance (docs/DESIGN.md §8.9.24(1)).
cpu_ep_vs_reference.at_scale_basis_note: max_ulp_at_scale_diff is None where the reference tensor has no finite nonzero scale: a residual divided by an undefined denominator is an absence, not a 0, and a 0 there would acquit
